goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in group-members.js.es6 the setupController sets controller.set('model', model) where model is the group object, then calls model.findMembers(). The findMembers() method in group.js sets 'members' property on the group object (self.setProperties({...members:...})). In the template group/members.hbs, the code iterates over 'members' ({{#each m in members}}). Since the controller's model is the group, and members is set on the group, the template should be able to access 'members' through the model. However, looking at the controller setup, it sets model to the group, and the template accesses 'members' directly. In Ember's ObjectController (which this extends based on the admin controller pattern), properties of the model are proxied. So accessing 'members' in the template would access model.members, which is set by findMembers(). This should work correctly. The finding suggests a mismatch but the code appears consistent - the group model has members set on it, and the template accesses members from that model.

Looking at the diff, line 11 shows `if (this.get("user_count") == 0) { return 0; }` in the currentPage computed property. The finding points to line 11 which is in the currentPage function. The code uses `==` for comparison which is loose equality in JavaScript. While using `===` would be more strict, this is a style/best practice issue rather than a real bug - comparing a number to 0 with `==` will work correctly. The user_count property is initialized as 0 (a number) and is set from server responses as numbers, so the loose equality comparison will function correctly. This is a style nit about preferring strict equality, not a real bug.

The finding references line 28 in groups_controller.rb and line 22 in admin/groups_controller.rb, but doesn't specify what the actual problem is. Looking at the diff, line 28 in groups_controller.rb is part of the members method which handles pagination properly. Line 22 in admin/groups_controller.rb is part of the create method. Without a specific description of what the problem is, I cannot verify if there's a real issue. The finding appears incomplete - it just references file locations without describing the actual defect.
